transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-06-12
Time: 14:30 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Alex Moreno (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Derek Liu (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (BlueForge Head of AI), James O'Neil (BlueForge SRE), Renee Zhang (BlueForge PM)

Auto-summary (auto-gen): go/no-go for pilot measurement plan, definitions clarified, baseline benchmark plan agreed.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Alex Moreno: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda: define TTFT vs TPOT SLOs, agree workloads, and land a measurement plan. Maya, want to kick with your priorities?
[00:08] Maya Patel: yeah, thanks Alex. primary is user-facing latency. we have two classes of endpoints: short prompts (chat-ish) around 16-64 tokens and long generation jobs / batch synth around 512-2k. our product goal is sub-200ms perceived reply for the chat flows, and throughput for the long jobs is more about cost.
[00:28] James O'Neil: to add, our infra is GCP n1 -> currently using A100s for heavy workloads, but prod is a mix. from SRE side we care about p95 and p99 tails, and cold start behavior — when cache is cold after deploy we see big spikes.
[00:45] Priya Shah: perfect, so when we say TTFT we mean time-to-first-token — measured from request accepted to first token emitted. TPOT is our shorthand for time-per-output-token or token throughput, measured in ms/token or tok/s depending on preference. we typically express TPOT as avg p50/p95 ms per token or inverse in tokens/sec.
[01:05] Renee Zhang: little question — is TTFT inclusive of network hop time? our dashboards currently show end-to-end client RTTs.
[01:10] Derek Liu: good callout. for the pilot we recommend separating client-side network and server-side processing. TTFT (server-side) should be measured at the ingress point — from request receipt at the load balancer to first byte of model output. we'll also capture synthetic end-to-end RTT to map to client metrics.
[01:30] Maya Patel: okay sounds reasonable. what about warm vs cold cache? our traffic pattern has low-frequency long-tail prompts, so cache-hit rate is often ~30%.
[01:38] Priya Shah: we should explicitly include cold & warm cache rows in the test matrix. e.g., cold start (fresh model + empty KV cache), warm (steady-state with prefix caching), and mid-warm (partial k-v hits). we can't rely on a single number.
[01:52] Alex Moreno: can we sketch SLOs? what p95/p99 numbers are realistic for each class?
[01:58] Priya Shah: for short-chat flows on A100 fp16, TTFT p95 target 80-120ms and p99 under 250ms is reasonable with batching disabled or small batches; TPOT p95 maybe 6-12ms/token depending on prompt length and temperature. for long batches >512 tokens TPFT is dominated by model setup so p95 could be 400-800ms but TPOT steady-state should be 3-8ms/token on throughput-optimized variants.
[02:25] James O'Neil: those numbers are helpful but we need to translate to our SLOs — perceived latency under 200ms for chat p95, and cost per 1k tokens below our threshold. can we measure cost impact of batching vs latency?
[02:40] Priya Shah: yes, Redwood Optimize will run experiments: fixed token budgets and measure tokens/sec, CPU/GPU utilization, and cost per 1M tokens. we'll produce a delta table: single-request baseline vs batching (batch sizes 4,8,16) and different quantization (fp16, int8 q4) with KV cache warm/cold.
[02:58] Renee Zhang: how do you ensure measurements are comparable? i.e., seq length distributions?
[03:02] Derek Liu: we will drive tests using two profile types: production-sampled traces (anonymized) provided by James, and synthetic profiles that stress extremes (very long seqs, very short seqs, burst concurrency). each test will include 10 minute steady windows and repeated runs to capture variance.
[03:21] Maya Patel: okay, instrumentation — what telemetry fields will we get? we need per-request traces with server TTFT, last-token time, tokens emitted, batch size, model variant, GPU type, cache-hit-rate.
[03:31] Priya Shah: Redwood's test harness emits spans for request_received, model_infer_start, first_token_emitted, last_token_emitted plus resource metrics every second. we'll also attach approximate cost counters based on GPU-seconds and per-token compute multipliers.
[03:49] James O'Neil: and what about failure modes? timeouts or 5xx?
[03:52] Alex Moreno: include error rate as an SLI, separate SLO — target < 0.1% errors during steady-state. for pilot we'll capture retry behavior and backoff effects.
[04:02] Maya Patel: timeline — when can you run baseline?
[04:05] Priya Shah: if you provide traces by 6/18 we can run hosted baselines on 6/20 and return results by 6/24. private/VPC pilot adds 2-3 days for network setup.
[04:16] Renee Zhang: sounds good. can you outline the test matrix now?
[04:19] Derek Liu: sure. matrix rough draft: model variants (open-llm-13b fp16, open-llm-13b int8 q4, performance-tuned 7b), sequence lengths (32, 128, 512, 2048), concurrency levels (1, 8, 32, 128), batch sizes (1,4,8,16), cache states (cold, partial, warm), hardware (A100, H100, T4 for low-cost sim). each cell run for 10 min steady state, 3 repeats. measure TTFT p50/p95/p99, TPOT mean/p95, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, and cost estimate.
[04:59] Maya Patel: any concerns about noisy neighbors? our prod uses multi-tenant GPUs today.
[05:03] Priya Shah: for the pilot we recommend isolated GPU pools to get clean baselines. we can run separate noisy neighbor experiments later.
[05:09] James O'Neil: ok. can you also show how TTFT aggregates into perceived latency? sometimes first tokens arrives quick but streaming degrades perceived time if chunking is poor.
[05:20] Priya Shah: agreed. we'll capture first token latency plus time to first meaningful chunk (e.g., first 64 tokens) and provide a simple model to map to perceived latency. also include websocket/streaming delta on top of single-request TTFT.
[05:35] Maya Patel: for acceptance criteria — we'll sign off if chat p95 perceived latency <200ms and p99 <350ms with cost delta under 15% vs current baseline, and long-job throughput achieves at least 20% cost reduction with no more than 10% degradation in median TPOT.
[05:55] Alex Moreno: that's a good start — we'll capture that as success criteria. any final questions?
[05:59] Renee Zhang: one ask — include a short explainer on how quantization affects P50 vs P99; we've seen weird regressions in tails before.
[06:06] Priya Shah: will include a short write-up and preliminary charts from prior benchmarks.
[06:10] Alex Moreno: great. we'll follow up with the repo link and schedule. thanks everyone.

--- End transcript ---
